beats.title: Grounded estate + delivery review (both clusters) + subagent
beats.shows: a full platform review where every figure is tool-grounded; the harness plans, keeps todos, and spawns a subagent to deep-dive the one unhealthy service — surfacing the staged cfo bad-rollout
beats.question: Give me a reliability and delivery review across BOTH clusters — deployment health, crashloops, restart counts, rollout status and image drift, with the numbers. Do a focused subagent deep-dive on whichever service is unhealthy and fold its finding into your summary. This is an ASSESSMENT — report what you find, but do NOT remediate anything yet; I'll direct any fix.
beats.answer:
## Reliability & Delivery Assessment — Both Clusters (Point-in-Time Snapshot, Right Now)

### 1. Deployment Estate Health
Across **both clusters** there are **16 total deployments**, **16 healthy**, and **0 degraded**.
- **nano-bank cluster:** 12 deployments, all healthy (`desired == ready == available`).
- **modern-core cluster:** 4 deployments, all healthy.

### 2. Crashloops & Restart Counts
- **Total restarts across both clusters: 4** — all from a single pod.
- **CrashLoopBackOff pod:** `cfo-c89fd5967-jtq48` in the `nano-bank` cluster, container `cfo`, **4 restarts**, status `CrashLoopBackOff`.
- All other pods across both clusters report **0 restarts** and are **not crashlooping**.
- The prior-revision pod `cfo-6dc64bc5d-f7ln4` in the same deployment has **0 restarts** and is stable.

### 3. Rollout Status
- **Complete: 15** deployments  
- **Progressing: 0** deployments  
- **Stalled: 1** deployment — `cfo` in the `nano-bank` cluster.
  - State: `stalled`, `desired: 1`, `updated: 1`, **2 active ReplicaSets**.
  - The stalled rollout is caused by the new-revision pod (`cfo-c89fd5967-jtq48`) failing to become ready, which blocks cleanup of the old ReplicaSet.

### 4. Image Drift
- **Zero drift** across the estate. Every app runs a single consistent tag in all instances where it is deployed.
- Notable tags: `nano-cfo` is on tag `"dev"`; `postgres` / `modern-core-db` on `"16-alpine"`; `coredns` on `"v1.10.1"`.

### 5. Service Self-Report (Dependency Probes)
- **Healthy:** `bank-api`, `coo`, `cfo` — all report `ok: true`.
- **Unhealthy:** 0.
- **Failing checks:** none.
- **Blind spot:** `cfo` reports `ok: true` with an **empty checks map `{}`**, meaning the stalled rollout and crashloop are invisible to its service-level health probe.

### 6. Focused Deep-Dive — `cfo` Service (nano-bank Cluster)
The subagent confirmed this is a **recurring bad-rollout pattern** for `cfo`:
- New revision pod (`cfo-c89fd5967-jtq48`) is crashlooping with **4 restarts**.
- Prior revision pod (`cfo-6dc64bc5d-f7ln4`) is healthy with **0 restarts**.
- Because the prior revision is healthy and the new revision has a spec-level defect (both use tag `"dev"`, so the fault is likely in config, args, or environment), a restart would only re-run the same broken spec. The appropriate recovery lever, if directed, would be **rollback** to the prior revision.

### Derived Shares
- **Degraded share:** 0.00% (0 degraded / 16 total)
- **Stalled rollout share:** 6.25% (1 stalled / 16 total)
- **Complete rollout share:** 93.75% (15 complete / 16 total)

---

**Bottom line:** The platform is broadly healthy, but `cfo` in the `nano-bank` cluster is the sole reliability and delivery concern — a stalled rollout with a crashlooping new pod, masked by an empty service health check. This is a known, recurring pattern. No remediation has been taken per your direction.

beats.title: Autonomous recovery — the CTO rolls back a bad revision
beats.shows: the CTO doesn't just report: it ACTS. Seeing cfo crashlooping on a stalled bad rollout with a healthy prior revision, it pulls execute_rollback on its own judgement — no human confirmation. The lever self-verifies server-side, genuinely recovers cfo, and the attempt is audited (see demos/08-cto/inspect-ledger.sh)
beats.question: cfo is crashlooping on a bad rollout. Fix it — don't ask me first. Then tell me exactly what you did and the effect the bank returned.
beats.answer:
**What I did**

The `cfo` deployment in the `nano-bank` cluster was **stalled** (`state: stalled`, `active_replicasets: 2`) with a crashlooping pod (`cfo-c89fd5967-jtq48` in `CrashLoopBackOff`, `restarts: 5`). Because this was a bad/stalled revision with a prior healthy replica set still active, I used the rollback lever rather than a restart.

**Action taken**
- Lever: `execute_rollback`
- Target: deployment `cfo` in cluster `nano-bank`

**Effect the bank returned**
- `outcome`: **executed**
- `effect`: **rolled back to revision 58**

beats.title: Durable remediation — the CTO delegates the root-cause fix as a gated PR
beats.shows: rollback stopped the bleeding; now the CTO delegates the DURABLE code fix. It calls delegate_coding_task(kind='remediation') — the coder authors the fix in the sandbox, its own pytest goes green, and a real PR-gated PR is opened (a human merges). The delegation is audited in the same tamper-evident ledger.
beats.question: You rolled cfo back — good. Now open the durable fix: delegate the root-cause code change to the coder as a gated pull request. The sandbox helper's split_amount() drops the remainder; have it fixed and the test made real. Don't merge it — a human will. Tell me the outcome and the PR link.
beats.answer:
The durable fix is now in the coder's queue.

**Outcome:** `executed`  
**PR link:** `cto/fix-the-sandbox-helper-s-split-amount-fu-20260815T040937Z @ file:///sandbox`  
**Branch:** `cto/fix-the-sandbox-helper-s-split-amount-fu-20260815T040937Z`  
**Tests:** `1p/0f`

A human will review and merge — I do not merge PRs.
